semantics: Field separator, default ','. univocity (delimiterString) and commons (String delimiter) accept multi-character delimiters; jackson accepts one char.
Character that encloses a value containing the delimiter, the quote or a line break, default '"'. commons (null) and jackson (disableQuoteChar) can switch quoting off; univocity always has a quote.

Character that escapes a quote (commons: also the delimiter and itself) instead of RFC 4180 doubling. Default: none in commons and jackson (doubling); univocity quoteEscape defaults to '"', i.e. doubling. FALSE FRIEND: univocity escapeChar is the TSV escape (dialect.tsv-escape).
univocity only: the character that escapes the quote-escape character itself (needed when quoteEscape is not the quote).
univocity only (parser and writer settings): process / write escape sequences in unquoted values. commons applies its escape character to unquoted values natively.

Line comment start. univocity: configurable char, default '#', detection switchable (commentProcessing); commons: configurable char, default none; jackson: '#' only ("hash comments"), on/off per schema or parser feature.
Record separator (1-2 chars in univocity). commons and jackson use it for output only and accept CR, LF and CRLF on input; univocity uses it for input and output.
Detect the input's line separator (univocity); report the first end-of-line seen (commons CSVParser.getFirstEndOfLine).
univocity only: the single normalized newline character that stands for the line separator while parsing/writing.
univocity only (parser and writer): replace line separators inside quoted values by the normalized newline (and back on write).
A delimiter after the last value: commons writes one (and tolerates it on read); jackson tolerates one extra empty trailing column on read.
univocity TSV: escape character for \t \n \r and itself, plus the letter that stands for an escaped tab. commons covers TSV with the TDF preset (no escapes).
univocity TSV (parser and writer): a line ending in the escape character continues the value on the next line.
univocity fixed-width: padding character, keep or strip padding, header alignment and padding.
univocity fixed-width: choose the field-length layout of a record by a lookahead/lookbehind value, with a wildcard character.
univocity fixed-width: records end at a newline, trailing characters skipped to the newline, a line separator written after each record.

Named dialect presets: commons CSVFormat.Predefined (DEFAULT, EXCEL, INFORMIX_UNLOAD, INFORMIX_UNLOAD_CSV, MONGODB_CSV, MONGODB_TSV, MYSQL, ORACLE, POSTGRESQL_CSV, POSTGRESQL_TEXT, RFC4180, TDF) and newFormat(delimiter); jackson's default schema.
Builder for an immutable dialect value (commons CSVFormat.Builder; jackson CsvSchema.Builder via rebuild). univocity settings are mutable beans instead.
The dialect value a reader or writer carries: univocity Format inside the settings bean; jackson CsvSchema as FormatSchema. commons: CSVFormat itself is the value.
Explicit column names. commons header() with no names means "read them from the first record" (header.from-first-record).
Take the column names from the first record of the input (and, for writers, write them first).
commons: the input starts with a header record that is skipped because names were given explicitly.
Name to index lookup after the header is known (commons CSVParser.getHeaderMap / getHeaderNames, CSVRecord.isMapped). univocity: Record and ParsingContext.headers; jackson: CsvSchema columns.
Policy for repeated header names: allow all, allow only empty ones, refuse.
commons: empty header names allowed or refused; jackson: fail when the header has fewer columns than the schema.
commons: header names matched ignoring case.
jackson: the header must equal the schema's column names.
jackson: reorder the schema's columns to the order found in the header.
univocity: read or write only selected (or all but excluded) columns by name or index, optionally keeping input order.
jackson: build and edit a typed column list (string, number, boolean, array columns).
Per-column metadata: name, index, declared type, array flag (jackson CsvSchema.Column); univocity RecordMetaData (types and conversions per column).
jackson: separator of the elements of an array-valued column inside one cell.
jackson: collect columns beyond the schema under one named property.
Derive columns from a Java type (jackson, POJO properties, optionally per view) or settings from annotated classes (univocity). jdk.m3: record components.
String that is read as null and written for null. Defaults: univocity null (empty unquoted value reads as null), commons none, jackson none.
Value for an empty quoted value "" (univocity parser), written for an empty value (univocity writer); jackson coerces "" to null.
Drop whitespace around unquoted values. Defaults differ: univocity true (read and write), commons false, jackson false.
Drop whitespace inside quotes (univocity). commons trim trims every value, quoted or not, on read and write.
univocity: keep the enclosing quotes in parsed values.
univocity: keep escape sequences in parsed values instead of resolving them.
univocity: treat the bit characters \0 and \1 as whitespace.
Skip empty (jackson: also blank) lines instead of reading empty records. Defaults: univocity true, commons true (DEFAULT format), jackson false.
Malformed quoting: univocity's five strategies for a quote that is not escaped; commons trailingData accepts characters after a closing quote (Excel compatibility).
commons: end of input inside a quoted value is accepted (Excel compatibility).
univocity: detect delimiter, quote and quote escape from a sample of rows; pluggable input analysis.
Rows shorter than the header: jackson fails or inserts nulls; commons reports it per record (CSVRecord.isConsistent).
jackson: ignore values beyond the schema's columns instead of failing.
Skip rows before reading: univocity N rows; jackson the first data row after the header.
univocity: stop after N records.
Input buffering: univocity buffer size and read-ahead thread; jackson access to the input source and release of buffered content.
Keep comment lines: univocity collects them in the context; commons attaches them to records, the header and the end of input.
Resource limits: univocity characters per value and columns per record (default 512); jackson StreamReadConstraints / StreamWriteConstraints.
univocity: callback that receives conversion / processing errors per record and decides to continue.
univocity: how much of the offending content an exception message shows (0 hides it).
Open a reader over a Reader, File, Path, URL or String (commons CSVFormat.parse and CSVParser.parse factories; univocity beginParsing; jackson ObjectReader with a schema from CsvMapper / CsvFactory).
univocity: parse the whole input, pushing every row to the configured processor callback.
Read all remaining records into a list.
Pull records one at a time: iterator, Stream, or next-record calls.
univocity: parse one line given as a String.
A record's values by index, header name or enum; size; to List or Map (commons CSVRecord). univocity Record (typed getters) and String[] rows; jackson binds rows to objects.
Where the reader or writer is: line, record number, character offset (univocity ParsingContext, record count of a writer; commons counters; jackson JsonLocation).
Open a writer over an Appendable, Writer, File or Path (commons CSVFormat.print / printer, CSVPrinter.getOut; jackson ObjectWriter with a schema). univocity: CsvWriter constructors.
Write one record (or format it to a String: commons CSVFormat.format, univocity *ToString).
Write many records (Iterable, arrays, column maps), optionally closing the output or returning Strings.
Build a record value by value and end it (commons print / println; univocity in-memory row then writeValuesToRow).
Write the header record (univocity automatically when headerWriting; commons printHeaders from JDBC metadata or printRecord of names).
Write comment lines (commons header comments before the data, printComment anywhere; univocity commentRow).

When output values are quoted: all, all non-null, minimal (only when needed), none, non-numeric (commons QuoteMode); per column, extra trigger characters, nulls, values containing the quote (univocity); always strings / empty strings / numbers, strict check (jackson).
How specials are escaped on output: jackson escapes the quote or control characters with the escape character, custom CharacterEscapes; univocity trusts already-escaped input.
Rows with fewer values than columns: univocity pads them to the header width; jackson may omit missing trailing columns.
univocity: write objects (beans, maps) through a RowWriterProcessor that converts them to rows.
Close and flush readers and writers; univocity closes its input automatically at the end (autoClosing); commons flushes on close (autoFlush).
univocity callback pipeline (Processor / RowProcessor: bean, column, master-detail, conversions) configured on the parser settings.
jackson-core JsonParser protocol over CSV (tokens, typed values). Kept as Jackson's own API; the jdk.m3 reader feeds it.
jackson-core JsonGenerator protocol over CSV. Kept as Jackson's own API; the jdk.m3 writer serves it.
jackson feature-flag and capability protocol (CsvParser.Feature / CsvGenerator.Feature masks, codec, mapper builder, version).
jackson: expose the record stream as one JSON array for databind.
Donor-internal helpers that are public only for subclassing or back-links (CSVRecord.getParser); no capability.
